title: A service's claims, merged with the platform's facts
description: This schema is a security boundary (ADR-0017 §6). It sees the merged values: the service's claims.yaml plus the system and environment objects the platform writes into helm.valuesObject. Every level is closed, so a key nobody listed is refused rather than ignored.

databases.description: Your databases, keyed by name. The name becomes part of the Cloud SQL instance name <system>-<name>, so it may use only lowercase letters and digits: no hyphen (ADR-0017 §5). At most two per System.

system.description: Written by the platform from the System's tenant file. A value you set here is replaced.

tier.description: The System's tier, approved by the platform in the systems repo. It is the entitlement that size L needs (ADR-0017 §6).

databases.description: In a standard-tier System, no database may be size L. Size L needs the System itself to be critical, which the platform approves in the systems repo.

engine.description: Postgres major version. Only the versions the platform supports are listed.

region.description: Where the data lives. Keep it in the cluster's region unless you have a reason not to.

size.description: A size class, not a machine type. S is shared-core, M is 2 vCPU / 7.5 GB, L is 4 vCPU / 15 GB and regional (high availability).

tier.description: How much the business loses if this database is down. Defaults to standard. Size L needs tier critical here AND a critical System.

backups.description: Daily automated backups, taken only while the instance runs, so a parked instance takes none. Point-in-time recovery comes only with size L. Defaults to true; only size S may turn backups off.

allOf.description: Size L needs tier: critical, written out.
Only size S may turn backups off.

environment.description: The environment's facts, from platform-config/environments/<env>.yaml. Every key is required and non-empty (ADR-0017 §8). This definition is identical in charts/system and charts/claims; CI checks that.
